news.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
news.lede: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier. While Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are still playing at 39 and 41 respectively, most football fans thought Ronaldinho belonged to another footballing era. That all changed in June, when Italian Serie C club, Ravenna, announced that the former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan forward would play for them in the upcoming season.

news.title: Ex-FCTA Spokesman Urges FIFA To Introduce Over-40 World Cup
news.lede: Former Spokesman of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), Nosike Ogbuenyi, has urged the World Football Governing body (FIFA) to introduce an Over-40 World Cup for retired football stars. Ogbuenyi made the call in Abuja after submitting a proposal for the competition to FIFA through the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) secretariat. He said the proposed tournament would enable football fans worldwide to continue enjoying the skills of legendary players beyond their active careers. He added that “the introduction of FIFA Over-40 World Cup will make the football-loving world to continue to watch the best of all time on the field of play for a longer period.”

news.title: FIFA reveal 240,000 abusive social media posts during 2026 Men’s World Cup
news.lede: FIFA have revealed that more than 240,000 abusive social media posts and comments were identified during the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup. The findings, released to coincide with World Mental Health Day on October 10, highlight the scale of online abuse directed at players, coaches, match officials and other tournament participants. FIFA’s Social Media Protection Service (SMPS) analysed more than 17 million posts and comments during the tournament, held in Canada, Mexico and the United States. Of those, 477,000 were referred for human review, with 240,000 verified as abusive.

news.title: Argentina were World Cup’s most targeted team online, says FIFA report
news.lede: Argentina were the most targeted national team on social media during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with accusations of referee favouritism, corruption and xenophobia among the main forms of abuse directed at the side, a FIFA report published on October 9 noted. The governing body’s Social Media Protection Service (SMPS) analysed more than 17.1 million posts and comments on X, Instagram, Facebook and TikTok between June 9 and July 20. Of those, 477,000 were referred for human review, with 240,000 verified as abusive. England were the second-most targeted team, followed by Spain, Brazil and Norway, the report found.

news.title: Former FCTA Spokesman Proposes FIFA Over-40 World Cup for Retired Stars
news.lede: The proposal aims to keep retired legends like Lionel Messi, Jay Jay Okocha, and other global icons in the public eye and contribute to the development of the sport after their professional careers end. A former spokesman of the Federal Capital Territory Administration , Nosike Ogbuenyi, has called on the Fédération Internationale de Football Association to introduce an Over-40 World Cup to enable retired football stars to continue showcasing their talents on the global stage. Ogbuenyi, an Assistant Editor with Premium Times, made the proposal in a submission to FIFA through the Nigeria Football Federation secretariat in Abuja on Thursday.
